candidates.name: ubdc-airbnb (Urban Big Data Centre)
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized, continuously-run scraper (Docker + Django/Celery) that has been collecting DAILY snapshots since 2020 of Airbnb listing property characteristics, booking calendars (day-by-day availability), booking policies, host info, and guest reviews for user-defined geographic areas. Method published/validated in PLOS One 2024 (Enhancing our understanding of short-term rental activity: a daily scrape-based approach for Airbnb listings, PMC10849255) which derives occupancy indicators from calendar-state changes. The actual accumulated dataset (30 UK/Scotland TTWAs, monthly estimates Jun-2021 to Dec-2023) is restricted to UBDC staff (researchdata.gla.ac.uk/2056) but the full scraping/estimation codebase is public on GitHub, so the method (daily calendar-diff -> occupancy/review-count series) is directly reusable against any market.
candidates.why_useful: This is the most rigorous public implementation of exactly the method needed for gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs from a free/buildable source) and this theme's review-count-as-stays-proxy angle: it operationalizes daily calendar diffing plus review accrual into an occupancy indicator, peer-reviewed, with a working codebase we could point at any of our 123 Inside-Airbnb markets if we wanted independent validation of our own stays index methodology.
candidates.size_hint: Full scraper codebase (~multiple Python modules, Docker Compose stack); underlying dataset itself is access-restricted, no row counts published
candidates.time_coverage: Scraping running continuously since 2020; published analysis window Jun 2021-Dec 2023
candidates.geography: User-configurable areas; published study covers 30 Scottish + 10 other UK Travel-to-Work Areas
candidates.license: check repo (not confirmed in this pass)
candidates.last_activity: not confirmed precisely; academic group repo, appears actively maintained as of 2024 publication

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Tom Slee's well-known (pre-Inside-Airbnb) Airbnb scraper, originally run 2014-2017 across many cities worldwide, storing room-level survey snapshots (listing, host, room type, price, overall_satisfaction/review count, reviews count, availability) in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS schema. The repo itself is an unmaintained scraping tool with no CSVs committed to GitHub; the actual historical CSV survey files (2014-2016, one file per city-scrape) are hosted externally on S3, linked from tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data.
candidates.why_useful: This is the single most cited pre-2015 / pre-Inside-Airbnb historical Airbnb snapshot archive that predates our current 13-city panel (Dec-2022 onward) by 6-8 years, directly answering the HIGH-value gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb-era dumps). Each survey snapshot carries a reviews-count field per listing that can be turned into an older review-accrual/stays proxy series for the same cities we already track.
candidates.size_hint: Multiple city-level CSV archives on S3, exact row counts not confirmed without downloading
candidates.geography: Multiple global cities (US, Canada, Europe); exact list on tomslee.net
candidates.last_activity: repo unmaintained since ~2017; still publicly readable

candidates.name: BlackFalconData-org/airbnb-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: No-browser scraper that pulls Airbnb reviews as flat rows (review text, star rating, date, reviewer name & location, language, host public reply) for any listing URL or an entire city, output as structured JSON. No data committed to the repo itself; updated Sep 2026 so actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: A working, recently-updated method for building a fresh review-date/review-count corpus per city if the team ever needs a more current stays-proxy panel than the frozen Inside Airbnb reviews.csv extracts; scraping airbnb.com directly is a ToS decision per repo rules so this is catalogued as method only, not run.

candidates.name: stayapi/airbnb-review-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python/Node scraper for Airbnb listing reviews with CSV export, no proxies/CAPTCHA handling needed, backed by the StayAPI service (50 free requests/month on the free tier).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative, permissively-licensed method for pulling review text+dates per listing if a small-sample validation of review-count-as-stays-proxy is needed; catalogued as method only (scraping airbnb.com is a ToS decision for a human).

candidates.name: Ankit-Peshin/airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Course/capstone project that runs NLP (bag-of-words, word2vec/embeddings) over a large Airbnb reviews corpus, reporting a resulting bag-of-words of 20M+ words after sampling ~30% of the full reviews dataset (implying an underlying corpus in the tens of millions of review tokens, likely Inside-Airbnb-derived, multi-city). Code (Airbnb_final_knit.rmd and related) shows the preprocessing/sampling pipeline rather than shipping a standalone dataset file.
candidates.why_useful: A reusable, already-tested large-scale NLP preprocessing pipeline for a multi-city reviews corpus at a scale close to what we would need to extend our 123-market reviews-based stays index or to mine review text for demand-adjacent signals (e.g., complaint/cancellation language, sentiment shifts) rather than just review counts.
candidates.size_hint: >20M-word bag-of-words from a 30% sample of the full review set (underlying corpus likely tens of millions of tokens / hundreds of thousands of reviews)

candidates.name: NLP-Text-Mining-Cultural-differences-between-Lisbon-and-Rio-de-Janeiro-in-Airbnb-Portuguese-reviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Master's thesis repo doing NLP/topic-modelling (LDA, bag-of-words, thematic coherence) comparing Portuguese-language Airbnb reviews from Lisbon (Inside Airbnb snapshot, Sep 2025) and Rio de Janeiro (Inside Airbnb snapshot, Sep 2026-adjacent). Uses Inside Airbnb reviews.csv for both cities as the raw corpus.
candidates.why_useful: A recent (2025-vintage) non-English, cross-market Airbnb reviews dataset+methodology; useful if the team wants a LatAm (Rio) reviews-text vintage newer than what we currently hold (our 123-market panel; Rio not in our named 13-city list), and a working non-English NLP pipeline that could be repointed at other Portuguese/Spanish-speaking markets for the LatAm gap (#7).
candidates.size_hint: Two city-level Inside Airbnb reviews.csv snapshots (row counts not confirmed)
candidates.geography: Lisbon, Portugal; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

candidates.name: andreaponti5/revscrap
candidates.what_it_holds: A Python Dash web app that scrapes reviews for both the Google Play Store and the Apple App Store for any given app, not Airbnb-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Generic, reusable method to build an Airbnb-mobile-app review-volume/rating-over-time series (a public engagement/download proxy) addressing gap #5 (app rankings/engagement history), which is otherwise hard to get free historical data for; would need to be pointed at the Airbnb app IDs on each store.

candidates.name: katacek/google-play-reviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Generic scraper that pulls Google Play Store app user reviews (name, date, text) into a dataset given an app URL/ID; not Airbnb-specific, no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as revscrap above: could be re-pointed at Airbnb's own Play Store listing to build a review-count/date-stamped engagement time series as a demand-adjacent signal (gap #5).

candidates.name: EpicSaber/airbnb-reviews-scraper (and sibling EpicSaber/airbnb-review-scraper, BigAnomaly/airbnb-reviews-scraper---low-cost)
candidates.what_it_holds: Thin GitHub wrapper/landing pages pointing to paid Apify actors for Airbnb review scraping; no code or data of substance committed to the repos themselves.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: confirms multiple commercial Apify-actor options exist for Airbnb review scraping (market/listing-wide), but nothing here is a usable open dataset or a real open-source method beyond an actor listing link. Flagged for completeness only.

notes: gh search repos hit the 6-call budget quickly with mostly low-value results (single-Kaggle-file tutorials, spammy zero-star scraper-marketing repos, Apify-actor landing pages) — the theme is thin on GitHub CLI alone; WebSearch surfaced the two genuinely high-value finds (UBDC's peer-reviewed continuous daily-scrape system, and Tom Slee's 2014-2017 pre-Inside-Airbnb archive). No true committed multi-million-row Airbnb reviews text corpus was found sitting directly in a GitHub repo (as opposed to pointing to Inside Airbnb or an S3/Apify host) — everything substantial is either a method/scraper or a pointer to an external host. Did not find any Reddit r/airbnb dump or Airbnb Community Center forum scraper on GitHub (searched, came up empty — worth another agent's pass with different terms, e.g. Arctic Shift / Academic Torrents Reddit dumps filtered for airbnb subreddit). Did not use gh search code at all (0/1 budget used) since promising leads came from WebSearch instead; a future scout could spend that one call on something like `gh search code "reviews_per_month" filename:*.csv` if a very targeted grep is wanted. UBDC's actual accumulated dataset is access-restricted to their staff, so it is method-only value for us, not a data pull.
